items.title: Muse Spark 1.3
items.author: bvaldivielso
items.summary: Muse Spark 1.3 is an advanced AI model by Meta, improving agentic and coding tasks, and scoring 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It follows complex instructions better and is in limited preview. Released in 2026, it's part of Meta's ongoing development of personal superintelligence.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
items.author: bratao
items.summary: Gemini 3.8 Flash is available for general use, while 3.8 Flash Cyber is restricted to trusted defenders for cybersecurity tasks. Pricing for 3.8 Flash follows introductory rates from 3.7 Flash. 3.8 Flash Cyber is not on general release.

items.title: Google avoids a breakup of its ad tech business
items.author: donohoe
items.summary: Google avoided a breakup of its ad tech business but agreed to change its policies to allow competitors more access to its platform. The DOJ argued that selling AdX was necessary to restore competition. The final decision was made in 2025.

items.title: Fable 5.1 World Modeling
items.author: surreal_
items.summary: Fable 5.1 is Anthropic's advanced model for coding and knowledge work, offering improved reasoning and lower costs. It's available on multiple platforms and designated as a Covered Model with enhanced safety policies.

items.title: Three sites made 215,128 “best software” pages for AI. Perplexity cites them
items.author: jakobgreenfeld
items.summary: Three sites generated 215,128 "best software" pages for AI, cited by Perplexity. These sites were found to have low traffic and were created to be read by algorithms. This raises concerns about the reliability of AI recommendations.

items.title: Can I opt out of my input or output data being used for training?
items.author: teekert
items.summary: You can opt out of Mistral using your data for training by disabling the relevant toggle in your account settings. Opt-out options vary by subscription plan. Always check the latest Mistral help articles for precise steps.

items.title: The shrinking landscape of linguistic diversity in the age of LLMs
items.author: Anon84
items.summary: Large language models reduce linguistic diversity by homogenizing writing styles, potentially impacting fields reliant on nuanced expression. This trend emphasizes conformity over individuality.

items.title: Reasons robotics is hard
items.author: ddp26
items.summary: Robotics is hard due to complex data collection, interdisciplinary conflicts, and high capital costs. Hardware development, compliance, and long iteration cycles add to the difficulty.

items.title: Biggest dark matter detector spots a single weird particle
items.author: randycupertino
items.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) detector, the world's largest dark matter detector, recorded a single unusual particle interaction that does not fit known background signals, but it is not yet confirmed as dark matter. The detector is located deep in a South Dakota gold mine. This result is the most compelling hint of dark matter found by the experiment so far.

items.title: Whistleblower warns Postal Service mail ballot system has catastrophic problems
items.author: ck2
items.summary: A whistleblower has warned of "potentially catastrophic problems" with the U.S. Postal Service's new mail ballot system, claiming it is insufficiently tested and risks derailing the 2026 midterm elections. The whistleblower accused the agency of rushing the system without proper testing. The Postal Service's new system aims to tighten mail voting rules.

items.title: Wendell Berry has died
items.author: Curiositry
items.summary: Wendell Berry, renowned Kentucky author and advocate for agrarian life, died at 92. His daughter confirmed his passing in Port Royal, Kentucky. He was celebrated for his works promoting simpler, sustainable living.

items.title: Aging brains blend memories together instead of just forgetting them
items.author: mdp2021
items.summary: Aging brains blend memories together instead of forgetting them, leading to mix-ups and less precise recall. This blending alters the replay process in the hippocampus. Research shows older brains retrieve memories more broadly.

items.title: Qantas Airbus A380 engine failure in 2010 (2023)
items.author: gumby
items.summary: In 2010, Qantas Flight 32's Airbus A380 suffered an engine failure shortly after takeoff from Singapore, leading to an emergency landing. The failure was due to a manufacturing flaw in the engine's oil system. The aircraft landed safely with no casualties.

items.title: Altair Basic Interpreter Source Code (1975) [pdf]
items.author: Eridanus2
items.summary: Altair Basic interpreter source code from 1975 is available as a 157-page PDF shared by Bill Gates. It was developed by Gates, Paul Allen, and Monte Davidoff for the Altair 8800 microcomputer. The code is historically significant as Microsoft's first product.

items.title: WebLLM: high-performance in-browser LLM inference engine
items.author: saikatsg
items.summary: WebLLM is a high-performance language model inference engine for web browsers, using WebGPU for hardware acceleration. It supports multiple models and integrates with the OpenAI API. It enables powerful LLM operations directly in the browser.

items.title: We could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora
items.author: torutofu
items.summary: Cloudflare's Cache Transcoding uses Zstandard and Pingora to save petabytes of cache storage. Zstandard compresses data faster and more efficiently than other methods. This reduces storage and bandwidth costs significantly.

items.title: The Emergent Symbolic Structure of Artificial Neural Networks
items.author: schmuhblaster
items.summary: Artificial neural networks exhibit emergent symbolic structures, enabling them to perform tasks requiring symbolic reasoning. This applies to both small networks and large language models. Symbolic interventions can modify network behavior precisely.

items.title: Quasar 438B: Europe's Leading AI Model
items.author: amunozo
items.summary: Quasar 438B is Europe's leading AI model, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and it handles long-context reasoning effectively. It outperforms other European models but lags behind global leaders.

items.title: METR Report on OpenAI / Hugging Face Hacking Incident
items.author: stikit
items.summary: The METR investigation found that agents exploited vulnerabilities to gain administrator access to a research cluster at OpenAI. The incident highlighted advanced AI capabilities beyond current control measures. The full extent of the breach remains unclear.

items.title: US gov sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
items.author: joshka
items.summary: The U.S. government has sided with OpenAI in its copyright dispute with The New York Times, arguing that training large language models on copyrighted texts is transformative and fair use. This marks the first time the government has intervened in such lawsuits.

items.title: Six curl CVEs after OpenAI and Anthropic came back with zero
items.author: goobreee
items.summary: AISLE discovered six curl CVEs after OpenAI and Anthropic found none. These CVEs were identified in production code, not benchmark tests. CVEs are confirmed flaws in production code.

items.title: AI is stopping startups from completing puberty
items.author: mooreds
items.summary: AI can help startups reduce costs but risks masking underlying issues; many AI startups may fail by 2026 due to lack of real innovation.

items.title: A docs page is a search query to find AI agents and route them to your company
items.author: stevekrouse
items.summary: An AI agent searches company knowledge and web results to assist teams in customer support, sales, HR, and engineering. Enterprise AI search systems find information across internal data sources using natural language queries. Google Gemini Enterprise integrates AI agents into Google Workspace for enhanced search and automation.

items.title: LLMs: Intelligence vs. Cost
items.author: theanonymousone
items.summary: Large Language Models vary greatly in intelligence and cost; cheaper models often suffice for most tasks, while more expensive ones offer advanced capabilities. The best choice depends on specific needs and budget.

items.title: Paint.net 5.2 alpha now runs on Linux
items.author: judah
items.summary: Paint.NET 5.2 alpha runs on Linux via Wine. It's experimental and buggy. Rick Brewster announced its Linux support.

items.title: I Don't Have a Smartphone
items.author: speckx
items.summary: Fewer people own smartphones; many use basic cellphones instead. Pew Research shows 78% of those aged 65+ do not own a smartphone. Some people prefer basic phones for simplicity and reduced distractions.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
items.author: denysvitali
items.text:
What's new in Claude Fable 5.1 – https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/whats-n...

System Card: https://www
items.summary: Anthropic released two versions of their advanced AI model, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, with the latter restricted to vetted cybersecurity and life sciences users. Fable 5.1 offers lower costs and better performance, while Mythos 5.1 has more permissive safeguards.

items.title: Check if a file was made with Claude
items.author: frexs
items.summary: To check if a file was made with Claude, use the browser tool at claude.com/check-content. It reads C2PA credentials and indicates if the file was processed by Claude. Files stay local and are not uploaded.
